The spin state is given as the spinor \(|\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} 3i \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\). The operator for the y-component of spin is \(S_y = \frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_y\), where \(\sigma_y = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix}\).

First, find the normalization constant:
\[
\langle\psi|\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} -3i & 4 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3i \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = (-3i)(3i) + (4)(4) = -9i^2 + 16 = 9 + 16 = 25.
\]

Next, compute \(\langle\psi|S_y|\psi\rangle\):
\[
\sigma_y |\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3i \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4i \\ 3i^2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4i \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
\[
\langle\psi|\sigma_y|\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} -3i & 4 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} -4i \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} = (-3i)(-4i) + (4)(-3) = 12i^2 - 12 = -12 - 12 = -24.
\]
\[
\langle\psi|S_y|\psi\rangle = \frac{\hbar}{2}(-24) = -12\hbar.
\]

The expectation value is:
\[
\langle S_y \rangle = \frac{\langle\psi|S_y|\psi\rangle}{\langle\psi|\psi\rangle} = \frac{-12\hbar}{25}.
\]

This matches option (C).

Answer: C
